About the tune

  • Music (1872): Lewis Hartsough (1828–1919)

Metre: 6.6.8.6 +.5.5.8.6.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune WELCOME VOICE by Lewis Hartsough (1828–1919). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about Welcome Voice

What is the doh of Welcome Voice?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Welcome Voice start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major), a pickup before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

What words can be sung to Welcome Voice?

Welcome Voice is in the metre 6.6.8.6 +.5.5.8.6: lines of 6, 6, 8, 6,, then, 5, 5, 8, 6 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is Welcome Voice in the public domain?

Yes. Lewis Hartsough died in 1919; the tune was first published in 1872. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
